bug_summary.title: Payment processor sends incorrect minor unit amounts for large decimal values, causing gateway rejections
symptoms: gateway rejections for transactions with non-zero cent values
bug_summary.expected_behavior: A payment of $9999.99 USD should result in 999999 minor units (cents) being sent to the payment gateway. The gateway should authorize and return a successful response.
bug_summary.actual_behavior: A payment of $9999.99 USD results in 999998 minor units being sent to the gateway. The gateway rejects amounts that are 1 cent off the expected value, returning INVALID_AMOUNT.

evidence.description: No logs provided — analysis based on bug report only

root_cause.hypothesis: float representation causes rounding errors due to to_minor_units() in Transaction class
root_cause.mechanism: The to_minor_units() function in the Transaction class loses precision when converting large decimal values to minor units, leading to incorrect amounts being sent to the payment processor.
root_cause.evidence_alignment: The repro result and failure surface point to the payments/processor.py file as the source of the issue, and the anomalies and affected files are consistent with this hypothesis.

patch_plan.summary: Modify to_minor_units() to use a more precise data type or implementation

files_to_change.change: use a more precise data type

patch_plan.code_change: Modify to_minor_units() to use a more precise data type or implementation

validation_steps: Step 1: Verify to_minor_units() function is working correctly

edge_cases: Test JPY (multiplier=1) — no subunit conversion needed
Test EUR and GBP amounts to ensure multiplier consistency
Test negative amounts (should be rejected before reaching to_minor_units)
